skill.name: url-routing-patterns
skill.description: Use when designing URL structures, slug generation, SEO-friendly URLs, redirects, or localized URL patterns. Covers route configuration, URL rewriting, canonical URLs, and routing APIs for headless CMS.

generated_query: I'm building a headless CMS for a multilingual tech blog. I have three content types: BlogPost, Category, and Author. I want SEO-friendly URLs: for posts, use `/blog/{category-slug}/{post-slug}`; for categories, `/blog/{category-slug}` (but only if it has at least one post); for authors, `/authors/{author-slug}`. Posts have a publication date, but I don't want dates in URLs. Categories can have parent‑child relationships, so URL hierarchy should reflect that (e.g., `/blog/programming/python`). I need to generate slugs from titles: lowercase, remove diacritics and special chars, replace spaces with hyphens, enforce a max length of 80 chars, and ensure uniqueness per content type (append `-1`, `-2` if needed). Also, when a post’s category changes, I need to redirect the old URL to the new one using a 301 permanent redirect. How should I design the route patterns, implement slug generation, and handle redirects?

edit_instructions.rationale: Without automatic redirect creation, the skill cannot handle the required 301 redirects when a post's category changes, leaving the user to manually manage redirects.
Removes the configurable MaxLength property, so the slug generator cannot be set to the required 80 chars.
Hardcodes maximum slug length to 100, making it impossible to enforce the 80‑character limit the user requires.
The skill now uses a static string instead of the actual dynamic category slug, so the URL pattern /blog/{category-slug}/{post-slug} will not work correctly.
The redirect type is changed from permanent to temporary, failing the user requirement for a 301 redirect that preserves SEO equity.
Removes the content type filter from slug uniqueness check, making slugs unique globally instead of per content type, which fails the user's requirement.
Removing the unique slug generation method means slugs might conflict, violating the user's uniqueness requirement per content type.
Removing category and parent path tokens prevents hierarchical URL structures, which the user needs for parent-child category relationships.
Changing the redirect to temporary (302) instead of permanent (301) fails the user's requirement for SEO-friendly 301 redirects when category changes.
Removing the uniqueness loop means slugs may collide across content types, violating the query's requirement for unique slugs per content type with incremental suffixes.
Deleting the max length enforcement allows slugs longer than 80 characters, ignoring the query's explicit constraint of maximum 80 characters.
Removing the parent path handling prevents generating hierarchical URLs for nested categories (e.g., /blog/programming/python), which the query requires for parent-child category relationships.
Without the uniqueness loop, slugs will not be made unique per content type, breaking the requirement to append -1, -2 when duplicates occur.
